question.:question/problem:
A rinse tank initially holds $240\,\text{L}$ of water containing $9\,\text{kg}$ of dissolved dye.
A solution containing $0.05\,\text{kg/L}$ of dissolved dye is pumped into the tank at a rate of $16\,\text{L/min},$ while the completely mixed water is drained out at a rate of $24\,\text{L/min}.$ If the amount of dye $Q(t),$ in kilograms, in the tank $t$ minutes after pumping begins is given by

$$
Q(t)=\alpha \,(1-\frac{t}{30})+\beta {(1-\frac{t}{30})}^{3}
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants, what is the value of $\alpha -\beta ?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $Q$ be the amount of dissolved substance in the tank at time $t,$ in minutes. The amount entering minus the amount leaving gives
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}.$$
The units of these rates are $\text{kg/min}.$

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which substance enters the tank.
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{in}}&=(0.05\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\cdot(16\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\\
&=(0.05\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\cdot(16\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\\&=0.8\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which substance exits the tank.
The volume is
$$V(t)=240+16t-24t=(240-8t)\,\text{L}.$$
The concentration is $\frac{Q}{240-8t}\,\text{kg/L}.$ Hence,
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{out}}&=(24\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{240-8t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\\
&=(24\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{240-8t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\\
&=\frac{24Q}{240-8t}\,\text{kg/min}=\frac{3Q}{30-t}\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}&=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}\\&=0.8-\frac{3Q}{30-t}.\end{aligned}$$
Thus,
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{3}{30-t}Q=0.8.$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.
This is a first-order linear equation with variable coefficients. So we find the general solution using an integrating factor:
$$\begin{aligned}I(t)&=e^{\int 3/(30-t)\,dt}\\&=e^{-3\ln|30-t|}\\&=e^{\ln (30-t)^{-3}}\\&=(30-t)^{-3}.\end{aligned}$$
Multiplying both sides by $I(t)=(30-t)^{-3}$ yields
$$\begin{aligned}(30-t)^{-3}\cdot(\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{3}{30-t}Q)&=(30-t)^{-3}\cdot 0.8\\
(30-t)^{-3}\frac{dQ}{dt}+3(30-t)^{-4}Q&=0.8(30-t)^{-3}\\\frac{d}{dt}(Q(30-t)^{-3})&=0.8(30-t)^{-3}.\end{aligned}$$
Now, we integrate with respect to $t:$
$$\begin{aligned}\int\frac{d}{dt}(Q(30-t)^{-3})\,dt&=\int 0.8(30-t)^{-3}\,dt\\Q(30-t)^{-3}&=0.8\cdot\frac{1}{2}(30-t)^{-2}+C\\Q(t)&=0.4(30-t)+C(30-t)^{3}.\end{aligned}$$
Note that $C$ is a constant of integration.
The initial condition is $Q(0)=9.$ Thus,
$$\begin{aligned}0.4(30-0)+C(30-0)^{3}&=9\\
12+C(30)^{3}&=9\\C(30)^{3}&=-3\\C&=- \frac{1}{9000}.\end{aligned}$$
Finally, we obtain the following expression for $Q(t):$
$$Q(t)=- \frac{2 t}{5} - \frac{\left(30 - t\right)^{3}}{9000} + 12.$$
Writing this in the supplied normalized form gives
$$Q(t)=12(1-\frac{t}{30})-3(1-\frac{t}{30})^{3}.$$
Finally, we have $\alpha=12,\beta=-3,$ and
$$\alpha-\beta=12-(-3)=15.$$

question.:question/problem:
A fermentation vat initially holds $240\,\text{L}$ of liquid containing $9\,\text{kg}$ of dissolved nutrient.
A feed solution containing $0.05\,\text{kg/L}$ of the nutrient is pumped into the vat at a rate of $8\,\text{L/min},$ while the completely mixed liquid is drained out at a rate of $4\,\text{L/min}.$
Find, rounded to two decimal places, the amount of nutrient in the vat $5$ minutes after pumping begins.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $Q$ be the amount of dissolved substance in the tank at time $t,$ in minutes. The amount entering minus the amount leaving gives
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}.$$
The units of these rates are $\text{kg/min}.$

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which substance enters the tank.
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{in}}&=(0.05\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\cdot(8\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\\
&=(0.05\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\cdot(8\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\\&=0.4\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which substance exits the tank.
The volume is
$$V(t)=240+8t-4t=(240+4t)\,\text{L}.$$
The concentration is $\frac{Q}{240+4t}\,\text{kg/L}.$ Hence,
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{out}}&=(4\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{240+4t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\\
&=(4\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{240+4t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\\
&=\frac{4Q}{240+4t}\,\text{kg/min}=\frac{1Q}{60+t}\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}&=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}\\&=0.4-\frac{1Q}{60+t}.\end{aligned}$$
Thus,
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{1}{60+t}Q=0.4.$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.
This is a first-order linear equation with variable coefficients. So we find the general solution using an integrating factor:
$$\begin{aligned}I(t)&=e^{\int 1/(60+t)\,dt}\\&=e^{1\ln|60+t|}\\&=e^{\ln (60+t)^{1}}\\&=(60+t)^{1}.\end{aligned}$$
Multiplying both sides by $I(t)=(60+t)^{1}$ yields
$$\begin{aligned}(60+t)^{1}\cdot(\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{1}{60+t}Q)&=(60+t)^{1}\cdot 0.4\\
(60+t)^{1}\frac{dQ}{dt}+1(60+t)^{0}Q&=0.4(60+t)^{1}\\\frac{d}{dt}(Q(60+t)^{1})&=0.4(60+t)^{1}.\end{aligned}$$
Now, we integrate with respect to $t:$
$$\begin{aligned}\int\frac{d}{dt}(Q(60+t)^{1})\,dt&=\int 0.4(60+t)^{1}\,dt\\Q(60+t)^{1}&=0.4\cdot\frac{1}{2}(60+t)^{2}+C\\Q(t)&=0.2(60+t)+C(60+t)^{-1}.\end{aligned}$$
Note that $C$ is a constant of integration.
The initial condition is $Q(0)=9.$ Thus,
$$\begin{aligned}0.2(60+0)+C(60+0)^{-1}&=9\\
12+C(60)^{-1}&=9\\C(60)^{-1}&=-3\\C&=-180.\end{aligned}$$
Finally, we obtain the following expression for $Q(t):$
$$Q(t)=\frac{t}{5} + 12 - \frac{180}{t + 60}.$$
Finally, the amount in the tank $5$ minutes after pumping begins is
$$\begin{aligned}Q(5)&=0.2(60+5)-3(\frac{60}{60+5})^{1}\\&=13-3(\frac{12}{13})^{1}\\&\approx 10.23\,\text{kg}.\end{aligned}$$
This is rounded to two decimal places.

&=(0.05\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\cdot(8\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\\&=0.4\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which substance exits the tank.
The volume is
$$V(t)=240+8t-4t=(240+4t)\,\text{L}.$$
The concentration is $\frac{Q}{240+4t}\,\text{kg/L}.$ Hence,
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{out}}&=(4\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{240+4t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\\
&=(4\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{240+4t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\\
&=\frac{4Q}{240+4t}\,\text{kg/min}=\frac{1Q}{60+t}\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}&=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}\\&=0.4-\frac{1Q}{60+t}.\end{aligned}$$
Thus,
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{1}{60+t}Q=0.4.$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.
This is a first-order linear equation with variable coefficients. So we find the general solution using an integrating factor:
$$\begin{aligned}I(t)&=e^{\int 1/(60+t)\,dt}\\&=e^{1\ln|60+t|}\\&=e^{\ln (60+t)^{1}}\\&=(60+t)^{1}.\end{aligned}$$
Multiplying both sides by $I(t)=(60+t)^{1}$ yields
$$\begin{aligned}(60+t)^{1}\cdot(\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{1}{60+t}Q)&=(60+t)^{1}\cdot 0.4\\
(60+t)^{1}\frac{dQ}{dt}+1(60+t)^{0}Q&=0.4(60+t)^{1}\\\frac{d}{dt}(Q(60+t)^{1})&=0.4(60+t)^{1}.\end{aligned}$$
Now, we integrate with respect to $t:$
$$\begin{aligned}\int\frac{d}{dt}(Q(60+t)^{1})\,dt&=\int 0.4(60+t)^{1}\,dt\\Q(60+t)^{1}&=0.4\cdot\frac{1}{2}(60+t)^{2}+C\\Q(t)&=0.2(60+t)+C(60+t)^{-1}.\end{aligned}$$
Note that $C$ is a constant of integration.
The initial condition is $Q(0)=12.$ Thus,
$$\begin{aligned}0.2(60+0)+C(60+0)^{-1}&=12\\
12+C(60)^{-1}&=12\\C(60)^{-1}&=0\\C&=0.\end{aligned}$$
Finally, we obtain the following expression for $Q(t):$
$$Q(t)=\frac{t}{5} + 12.$$
Finally, the amount in the tank $5$ minutes after pumping begins is
$$\begin{aligned}Q(5)&=0.2(60+5)\\&=13\\&\approx 13.00\,\text{kg}.\end{aligned}$$
This is rounded to two decimal places.
